statement:
% Book-local P07.1 obstruction, 20 September 2026.
% This isolated statement is not yet a live-book input and makes no novelty
% or priority claim.

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p071-trivalent-double-junction-obstruction}
Let $S$ and $T$ be node neighbourhoods in two exact trivalent
Chambert--Loir--Ducros stars.  Use outward coordinates
$r,s\in[0,R)$ on their branches, label both branch sets by
$\{1,2,3\}$, and write $o=(\eta_S,\eta_T)$.  On $S\times T$, let
$\mathcal G_0$ be the following local two-star generator sheaf.  A member
$g$ is real-valued, has smooth jointly convex restrictions $g_{ij}$ to the
nine branch rectangles, has common smooth restrictions on the two families
of node axes, and satisfies
\begin{align}
 \sum_{i=1}^3\partial_rg_{ij}(0,s)&=0
       &&(j\in\{1,2,3\},\ 0\leq s<R),
 \label{eq:p071-trivalent-first-balance}\\
 \sum_{j=1}^3\partial_sg_{ij}(r,0)&=0
       &&(i\in\{1,2,3\},\ 0\leq r<R).
 \label{eq:p071-trivalent-second-balance}
\end{align}
Let $\mathcal P$ be the smallest subsheaf containing $\mathcal G_0$ and
closed under local pointwise decreasing sequential limits.

Every $v\in\mathcal P$ satisfies the following mixed double-junction
inequality near $o$.  Take finitely many atoms
\[
 z_a=(p_{i_a}(r_a),q_{j_a}(s_a)),
 \qquad \lambda_a>0,
 \qquad \sum_a\lambda_a=1,
\]
in one product node chart.  If there are $M,N\geq0$ such that
\begin{align}
 \sum_{a:i_a=i}\lambda_ar_a&=M
       &&(i=1,2,3),
 \label{eq:p071-trivalent-first-moment}\\
 \sum_{a:j_a=j}\lambda_as_a&=N
       &&(j=1,2,3),
 \label{eq:p071-trivalent-second-moment}
\end{align}
then
\begin{equation}
                       v(o)\leq\sum_a\lambda_av(z_a).
 \label{eq:p071-trivalent-mixed-jensen}
\end{equation}
The assertion uses the usual extended-real convention and is automatic
when $v(o)=-\infty$.

This mixed condition is not implied by joint convexity on the nine branch
rectangles together with both one-factor star--line junction families.
Indeed, on $[0,R)^2$ define
\begin{equation}
 u_{ij}(r,s)=r+s-3\delta_{ij}\min\{r,s\}.
 \label{eq:p071-trivalent-obstruction-function}
\end{equation}
The nine functions glue to a continuous real-valued function $u$ on
$S\times T$.  Every $u_{ij}$ is jointly convex.  For each fixed second
branch $j$, $u$ satisfies every first-star--line junction inequality:
whenever $\lambda_a>0$, $\sum_a\lambda_a=1$,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{a:i_a=i}\lambda_ar_a=M\quad(i=1,2,3),
 \qquad s_0=\sum_a\lambda_as_a,
 \label{eq:p071-trivalent-first-separate-data}
\end{equation}
with all atoms in that branch, one has
\begin{equation}
 u(\eta_S,q_j(s_0))
       \leq\sum_a\lambda_a
             u(p_{i_a}(r_a),q_j(s_a)).
 \label{eq:p071-trivalent-first-separate-jensen}
\end{equation}
The symmetric second-star--line family also holds.  Nevertheless, taking
the three atoms $(p_i(\rho),q_i(\rho))$, each with weight $1/3$, for any
$0<\rho<R$, gives
\begin{equation}
 u(o)=0> -\rho
   =\frac13\sum_{i=1}^3u(p_i(\rho),q_i(\rho)).
 \label{eq:p071-trivalent-obstruction-violation}
\end{equation}
Consequently $u\notin\mathcal P$ near $o$.  Thus any comparison class for
the genuinely branched two-star case must include mixed double-junction
conditions; iterating the two one-star comparison tests is insufficient.
This proposition does not assert that the mixed conditions are sufficient,
and it does not retire P07.1.
\end{proposition}
proof:
\begin{proof}
We first prove the necessary inequality for a smooth generator.  Put
\[
 c=g(o),\qquad
 \alpha_i=\partial_rg_{ij}(0,0),\qquad
 \beta_j=\partial_sg_{ij}(0,0).
\]
The common axis restrictions make $\alpha_i$ independent of $j$ and
$\beta_j$ independent of $i$.  Evaluating
\eqref{eq:p071-trivalent-first-balance} and
\eqref{eq:p071-trivalent-second-balance} at the double node gives
\begin{equation}
                         \sum_i\alpha_i=0,
                  \qquad \sum_j\beta_j=0.
 \label{eq:p071-trivalent-linear-balances}
\end{equation}
Joint convexity on the $(i,j)$ branch rectangle supplies the supporting
plane inequality at its corner:
\begin{equation}
 g_{ij}(r,s)\geq c+\alpha_ir+\beta_js.
 \label{eq:p071-trivalent-supporting-plane}
\end{equation}
Multiply \eqref{eq:p071-trivalent-supporting-plane} at $z_a$ by
$\lambda_a$ and sum.  The two moment identities and
\eqref{eq:p071-trivalent-linear-balances} give
\[
 \sum_a\lambda_ag(z_a)
 \geq c
   +M\sum_i\alpha_i+N\sum_j\beta_j
 =c.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:p071-trivalent-mixed-jensen} at stage zero.

The property is local at $o$, is preserved by restriction, and passes to a
pointwise decreasing limit.  For the last assertion, if the limiting value
at $o$ is finite, pass to the limit in the finite weighted sum; if it is
$-\infty$, the inequality is automatic.  The same observation survives
sheafification because one member of a local cover contains $o$.  A
transfinite induction through the generated hierarchy, or equivalently the
minimality of $\mathcal P$, proves the mixed inequality for every member of
$\mathcal P$.

We now audit the explicit function.  Since
\begin{equation}
 r+s-3\min\{r,s\}
       =\max\{-2r+s,r-2s\},
 \label{eq:p071-trivalent-diagonal-convexity}
\end{equation}
the diagonal branch functions are maxima of two affine functions and hence
are jointly convex.  The off-diagonal branch functions are affine.  At
$s=0$ every branch function equals $r$, and at $r=0$ every branch function
equals $s$.  They therefore glue continuously with common axis values.

Fix a second branch $j$ and data as in
\eqref{eq:p071-trivalent-first-separate-data}.  On the node axis one has
\[
                         u(\eta_S,q_j(s_0))=s_0.
\]
Hence
\begin{align*}
 &\sum_a\lambda_a
       u(p_{i_a}(r_a),q_j(s_a))-u(\eta_S,q_j(s_0))\\
 &\qquad=
   \sum_a\lambda_ar_a
      -3\sum_{a:i_a=j}\lambda_a\min\{r_a,s_a\}\\
 &\qquad=3M
      -3\sum_{a:i_a=j}\lambda_a\min\{r_a,s_a\}\\
 &\qquad\geq
   3M-3\sum_{a:i_a=j}\lambda_ar_a=0.
\end{align*}
This proves the complete first-star--line family, including unequal radii
and a varying line coordinate.  Interchanging the two factors proves the
second family.

Finally, for the three diagonal atoms of
\eqref{eq:p071-trivalent-obstruction-violation}, both branchwise radial
moments equal $\rho/3$.  Thus
\eqref{eq:p071-trivalent-first-moment} and
\eqref{eq:p071-trivalent-second-moment} hold, whereas
\[
 u_{ii}(\rho,\rho)=2\rho-3\rho=-\rho.
\]
The mixed inequality fails.  The necessary part already proved excludes
$u$ from the full generated sheaf near $o$ and completes the proof.
\end{proof}
